text: Maya: quick heads up — noticed odd behavior in compact playground when streaming long responses. token meter will jump to a final value and then disappear if you Regen or quick-insert from the prompt library mid-stream. reproducible with large code blocks. Alex: which composer? compact rail or full composer? Maya: compact convo rail (playground compact). happens more with chunked streams. also repro if you do a prompt-library quick-insert while streaming. R Cook: i've hit this. root cause looks like we flush final token count when a termination event happens, but stream chunks still come in and trigger a clear path. race between chunk render and finalize. Jenna: accessibility flag — aria-live updates are getting spammed on every chunk. screen readers read repeated changes which is noisy. we should not announce intermediate counts. Maya: UX suggestion: show a subdued "live" counter that is aria-hidden, update it visually but throttled. then reveal/announce the final counter once streaming completes. reduces noise and layout churn. Alex: sketch of markup idea: ``` ~430 Final: 430 / 4096 ``` R Cook: add 500ms throttle on visual updates to cut reflows. also debounce state transitions so we don't flip to final then immediately clear. Sam: quick-insert behavior question: current flow cancels streaming and we lose partial output. is that acceptable? i'd rather we not silently drop content. Maya: agreed. options: queue the prompt insert and show a toast, soft-insert into composer while stream continues, or cancel-and-apply immediately. dropping partials sucks. Jenna: preference is queue + toast for clarity. short toast copy: "Prompt queued to insert — stop streaming to apply". add an "Undo" action on the toast. R Cook: implementation note: simplest approach is client-side stash + flag. when user quick-inserts, stash the prompt and show toast. on next stop/regenerate event, merge stash into composer. server doesn't need to change. Maya: accessibility nit: the Stop button label is just "Stop" — screen readers lack context. change to "Stop streaming response" and add a tooltip showing shortcut (Esc). ensure the label is not visually verbose but has accessible name. Alex: also fix keyboard focus disappearing after stop — we lose focus ring on the control. must persist focus or move it predictably (e.g., to composer). accessibility-bot: contrast issue: token pill color (#7B61FF on #FFFFFF) fails AA for small text. use a darker fill or bold white text to meet contrast. Maya: i'll document the interaction: live visual throttle 500ms, live counter aria-hidden, final counter aria-live polite + aria-atomic true, queued-insert flow with toast + undo, stop-button accessible label + tooltip. Jenna: i'll update Figma with dual-counter visuals, stop copy change, toast design and keyboard hint (Esc to stop, Ctrl+Enter to submit). will attach link here when ready. R Cook: i'll own a short spike to prototype throttle + queued-insert behavior. estimate 2 days. will report perf before/after reflows. Maya: thanks. i'll post the figma link and the interaction doc in this thread when done. :thumbsup:
